Multiply 0.78 by these to get each member's own-industry share of its EU-channel military aid.

MDA.reasoning: Donor money for Moldova's refugee response, by year: low = FTS flows recorded against the Ukraine RRP with destination Moldova (USD 636m 2022-25, 2022 incl. a pro-rata share of multi-country flows); central = the same year profile scaled to UNHCR's 'over USD 785m' 2022-25 total (x1.23; FTS misses some partner funding); high = central x1.15 for bilateral money outside the RRP (EU/US grants to ministries, e.g. NHIC health coverage financed via IOM/UNICEF/UNFPA). 2026: UNHCR's own USD 64m was 28% funded by April; RRP USD 116m; assumed USD 30/50/70m for the year. Donor funding (EUR ~0.35bn in 2022, ~0.16bn in 2023 and 2024) is larger than the modelled host cost in refugees.json for those years (central EUR 0.08-0.14bn), and Moldova's own budget outlays were small (MDL ~387m, ~EUR 19m, from emergency funds by July 2022). About 31% of RRP target beneficiaries are vulnerable Moldovans, and part is agency overhead, so donor money is not all refugee cost. Share of total refugee-related spending in Moldova paid by donors: 0.6-0.95, central 0.8. Use: Moldova's own (net) cost = max(modelled cost x (1 - donor_share), small government outlays) - do not count donor-funded parts for Moldova and the donors at the same time.
